To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

OSM stimulates STAT3 activation, which enhances the expression/activation and secretion of MMP2 and the production of VEGF in human and canine O SA cells, ultimately promoting their invasive behavior and tumor vascularization.
OSM stimulation of canine and human osteosarcoma (OSA) cell lines induces phosphorylation of STAT, Src, and Jak2, resulting in enhanced expression and activity of MMP2, VEGF, and invasive behavior.
OSM is a potent inducer of MMP2 and angiogenic factors in canine and human OAS cell lines and tumor samples, and OSM stimulation of OSAs results in increased invasion and angiogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the STAT3 signaling pathway in osteosarcomas.
the development of a novel, non-toxic, anti-cancer agent for the treatment of osteosarcoma.
the role of the cytokine Oncostatin M in osteosarcomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
OSM and STAT3 signaling are potential therapeutic targets for the treatment of osteosarcoma, particularly in those tumors that express the OSMR.
our data indicate OSM is a potent stimulator of OSA cell invasion and angiogenesis, which may represent a novel therapeutic target in OSA.
the OSM/OSMR axis is activated in OSA, and that this results in STAT3 activation, which in turn promotes MMP2 activity and invasion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

OSM is expressed in canine and human Osteosarcoma, OSA cells express OSM receptors, and OSM stimulation of canine and human OAS cells results in STAT3 activation, MMP-2 expression, and enhanced VEGF production and invasion, which is attenuated by a small molecule STAT3 antagonist.

OSM and its receptors are overexpressed in canine and human osteosarcoma and that OSM stimulation of canine and human osteoblastic osteosarcoma cells results in enhanced STAT3 activity, increased MMP2 and VESGF expression and increased invasion.
we have shown that OSM is expressed by both canine and human osteosarcoma cells and that it can promote invasion of these cells by activating STAT3 and VEGF.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Oncostatin M, a cytokine that has not been previously investigated in osteosarcomas, is highly expressed in OSA tumors and cell lines, and is capable of inducing a pro-invasive phenotype in OSA cells.
Oncostatin M and the Oncostatin M receptor are expressed by canine and human osteosarcoma tumor samples and cell lines.

Oncostatin M is expressed in OSA tumor samples and OSA cell lines; OSM stimulation of these cells induces STAT3, MMP2, and VEGF; OSM stimulation enhances invasion through Matrigell; and OSM stimulation of canine and human OAS cell lines does not alter proliferation.
